body.statement: Under the sharp constant total-effect null, \(Q_{\tau,ij}=Y_{ij}(0,0)\) on \(U_P\), and for every \(0<\alpha<1\), \(\Pr\{p_\tau\le\alpha\mid P,Q_\tau\}\le\lfloor\alpha h(a,b)\rfloor/h(a,b)\le\alpha\). For the focal-dyad difference in means, \(1-D_z(X^{\mathrm{obs}})>0\) for every \(z\ne z^{\mathrm{obs}}\); if \(k_\alpha=0\), then \(\mathcal I_{1-\alpha}=\mathbb R\), while if \(k_\alpha\ge1\), then \(\mathcal I_{1-\alpha}=[t_{(k_\alpha)},\infty)\). Thus \(\Pr\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\).
body.justification: The result turns exact point-null validity into an effect-size confidence statement with the correct discrete endpoint.
body.gap: Luo et al. give general inversion conditions and Liu et al. treat the zero total-effect null, but neither derives this null-adjusted dyadic crossing formula.
body.consumer: The Platform O design can report an exact lower confidence bound for a constant dyad-level total effect under the stipulated exposure model.
